questions.question: Describe neurulation and notogenesis in frog embryo. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe neurulation and notogenesis in frog embryo. [K] / [CO4]
  • Neurulation: The dorsal ectoderm forms the neural plate, which folds and closes
  • to form the neural tube. The neural tube develops into the central nervous system.
  • Notogenesis: Formation of the notochord from axial mesoderm. The notochord
  • provides support and helps organize the development of the neural tube.
  • (Neurulation – 1 mark; Notogenesis– 1 mark)

  • • Prostate gland: Adds fluid containing citrate, enzymes and other substances that support
  • sperm function and contribute to semen liquefaction.
  • • Cowper's (bulbourethral) glands: Secrete mucus-like pre-ejaculatory fluid that lubricates the
  • urethra and helps neutralize residual acidity.
  • • Overall role: These secretions combine with sperm and other reproductive tract fluids to
  • form semen, supporting sperm transport and function.
